title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 123
paragraphs: When Polycrates heard this he rejoiced and was ready to agree; and since, it seems, he had a great desire for wealth, he first sent Maiandrios son of Maiandrios, a native of Samos who was his secretary, to see it. This was the same man who, not long after these events, dedicated to the temple of Hera all the ornaments of the men's chamber in the palace of Polycrates—ornaments well worth seeing. Oroetes, having heard that the man sent to examine the treasure would soon arrive, did as follows: he filled eight chests with stones, except for a small space at the very top of each, and laid gold on top of the stones. Then he tied up the chests and kept them ready. So Maiandrios came, looked at them, and brought word back to Polycrates.
